ai_summary: Great Britain’s wind output currently stands at 14.9 GW, bolstered by an estimated Scottish wind output of 5.3 GW, which represents 52.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This strong renewable performance drives Scottish carbon intensity down to a pristine 0 gCO2/kWh, compared to 101 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, persistent transmission boundary constraints between Scotland and southern demand centers continue to severely restrict north-to-south export capability. Because the network cannot accommodate this abundant zero-carbon power, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 37.0 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £2,019,063. To replace this trapped renewable energy, thermal power stations closer to demand had to fire up, requiring an estimated 7,020,861 m3 of gas burned elsewhere to replace it and emitting an avoidable 12,933 tonnes of CO2. Annualising these figures highlights an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £737 million. Distributed across national electricity demand, this recurring system constraint increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £2.50/MWh, demonstrating the substantial consumer and environmental dividends to be unlocked by accelerating cross-border transmission upgrades.
